predecessors.name: Tang dynasty
predecessors.text: Xichuan (Chengdu, taken 891) and Dongchuan (taken 897), Shannan West (Xingyuan, 902) and the Jingnan prefectures of Kui, Zhong, Wan and En (903), all won by Wang Jian as a Tang governor before he…

successors.name: Later Tang
successors.text: Sichuan, western Hubei and parts of southern Gansu and Shaanxi, taken by the Later Tang in 925

ledger.x: 907: Wang Jian proclaims the Great Shu at Chengdu.
915: Shu takes Qin and Feng prefectures from Qi.
916: Shu storms Baoji and besieges Fengxiang.
916: Shu lifts the siege of Fengxiang.
916: Wang Jian renames the state Han.
918: the state takes the name Shu again, in Wang Jian's last year.

wars.name: Shu-Qi war
wars.outcome: Shu victory on the Qin and Feng prefectures (autumn 915) and Baoji (autumn 916); the Fengxiang siege was lifted, leaving Qi a rump around its capital.

wars.name: Joint Shu-Qi attack on Chang'an
wars.outcome: Failed: the allied armies withdrew ('Qi forces were defeated by Liu Zhijun at Mu Valley'); no border moved.

wars.name: Later Tang conquest of Former Shu
wars.outcome: Later Tang victory: 'When the main Later Tang forces under Li Jiji arrived at Chengdu, Wang Yan formally surrendered'; the Former Shu ended in 925 and Wang Yan and his family were executed in 926.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on any opened page.
